routes.description: The Amazon restaurant-island hop: hourly cooperative lanchas today (15 min, R$12/leg) to Combu's over-water restaurants inside a state environmental protection area. Straight crossing of the Guamá river; haversine 1.2 nm + berth approach. The market's most iconic short corridor — silent, zero-wake arrival is the whole point.

Showcase-waterfront to lunch-island spur: no scheduled service today (tourists cab to Praça Princesa Isabel). Haversine 3.4 nm + ~1 nm coastal-wrap margin because the sea path rounds the Ver-o-Peso point from the Baía do Guajará into the Guamá river.
The orla corridor linking the two rebuilt COP30-legacy terminals; Geladão Fluvial services already call at both. Haversine 8.5 nm + margin along the gently curving Guajará shoreline.
The Geladão Fluvial workhorse: ~20-min municipal water-bus to the car-free island, R$4.60 weekdays. Haversine 4.4 nm, effectively direct across the Baía do Guajará past Outeiro's north tip.
The new direct Belém–Cotijuba line launched for July 2026 by the prefecture. Haversine 10.9 nm + ~1 nm wrap where the path clears the western shore of Ilha de Caratateua (Outeiro).

The beach express up the Baía do Guajará: weekend Geladão Fluvial today (220-pax lancha, ~1h40 via Icoaraci, R$20). Destination BP coordinate is null; distance estimated from the candidate Mosqueiro pier (haversine 16.6 nm) + wrap margin north along Mosqueiro's west coast to the Vila trapiche — RE-COMPUTE once the Tavernard trapiche coordinate is confirmed. Genuinely iconic locally; held at non-signature pending coordinate confirmation.

One of Pará's busiest regulated lines: Arapari's hourly ~62-pax lanchas, 45–60 min tide-dependent, R$17.58–18. Origin BP coordinate null (new terminal); distance computed from the Cidade Velha waterfront candidate pier: haversine 7.5 nm + ~3.5 nm coastal-wrap margin because the direct line crosses Ilha das Onças — the navigable path wraps south of the island via the furos. RE-COMPUTE on coordinate confirmation.

The Marajó vehicle-ferry lane (regulated fares R$24.80 pax, ~3h today) — the slow gateway a foiling passenger service leapfrogs. Haversine 22.6 nm + margin for the open Baía do Marajó crossing; largely direct water.

The buffalo-island express: today's 2h fast lanchas (R$61.17) and 3h ships to the capital of the world's largest river island. Haversine 42.7 nm + ~5 nm wrap: the route exits the Baía do Guajará past Mosqueiro and crosses the open Baía do Marajó before entering the Paracauari river mouth. Well inside the 70 nm envelope but the market's longest scheduled electric leg — the win over incumbent 25-kn lanchas is smoothness, silence and zero diesel, not headline speed.
Short beach-district spur across the Furo do Maguari mouth to Outeiro (bridge-linked; boat service lapsed after the bridge, revived interest around the COP30 Outeiro port). Haversine 1.0 nm, direct.
